# Success

<!--
Projects should have a definition of done that is measurable, and a
thorough understanding going in of what the risks are to delivery
-->

## Definition of Done

<!--
What does success look like?
-->

The project will be complete when I have published a tagged Arity release and
met the following criteria:

Language-server reliability
:   Tests show that Arity resolves shared documentation, reports undocumented
    parameters, and handles references and call hierarchy consistently for
    quoted function names. Renaming produces valid R syntax or Arity refuses the
    operation.

Package knowledge

:   At least 100 versioned indexes are published, with a documented schema and
    working weekly updates. For a package to count toward the target, its index
    must include arguments, defaults, and help for at least 80% of its exported
    functions. Export lists must match R's results for the same versions.
    Sampled arguments, defaults, and help must match or be withheld, and missing
    fields will be reported.

    Tests show completion details, hover information, and signature help without
    local installation, including packages outside the bundle. They also verify
    diagnostics for deprecated and defunct functions, covering supported
    declarations and local shadowing. The same tests pass offline after prefetch.
    With identical source, configuration, and cached metadata, name resolution and
    diagnostics agree between the editor and CLI.

Validation and adoption
:   I have published workflows and before-and-after results for ten packages,
    including checks in VS Code and Neovim, along with editor and CI guides and
    maintenance instructions. The release passes the existing workspace and
    corpus checks with no unexplained regressions.

## Measuring Success

<!--
How will we know when success is achieved, what markers can we use
along the way
-->

The report will compare diagnostics and response times before and after the
project using the ten package workflows. I will classify sampled diagnostic
findings as defects, false positives, or unresolved cases, and report remaining
limitations and any new regressions. For metadata, I will report coverage,
accuracy, how current the data is, and extraction failures, with deprecation
coverage reported separately. The report will document the versions,
configuration, and measurement setup so others can reproduce the comparison.

Feedback on the prerelease may add to these results, but completion will not
depend on download counts or volunteer participation.

## Future Work

<!--
How could this be extended / developed in the future by yourself
and/or the community in general?
-->

Future work could cover more packages, select exact versions from a project's
lockfile, support the CRAN Archive with package metadata from
[ALLPACKAGES](https://github.com/r-hub/allpackages), and use runtime tracing.
These are outside the scope of this grant.
